title: Crash, Coco, and the Bazooka Brigade
synopsis: Crash and Coco crash the battle as the annoying new arrivals, and the fight quickly turns into a chaotic arsenal showdown of Super Kicks, bazookas, and a howitzer or two. One combatant proudly reveals they've named their sixty-foot worm "Snakey," to everyone's disbelief, while another narrator daydreams of becoming the family's next Beam Master. Playful trash talk and misfired attacks carry the skirmish to its close.

title: Lunch Break and the Mimic Attack
synopsis: After a literal lunch-break interruption, the battle resumes with a dangerous copycat foe who mimics every attack thrown at her, countering Hyper Beams and Confusion moves right back at her attackers. The narrators dissolve into giggly chaos over dizziness, a "Shiny attack," and a bit where the villain declares herself the strongest of the whole gang before both sides claim to have failed.

title: The Crayon Thief's Fusion Trick
synopsis: A Fusion Attack and some very literal color-draining villainy take center stage, as one fighter threatens to suck all the color out of an opponent like a crayon. Amid rolly-polly jokes, a food-based aside, and a boast about a move called "Big Bashy Pringles Bash," the narrators keep tripping over each other's attack names as much as their toys trip over the battlefield. A tail catches fire just as the segment cuts off.

title: Evil Tigger's Secret Message
synopsis: Makuta sends an "Evil Piglet" and then an "Evil Tigger" to intercept a message, with Tigger cheerfully chanting "Happy day" while carrying out his dark orders. The narration wanders into real-life tangents about weekend plans and a Friday night show before snapping back to a squeeze-attack skirmish. It's a short, giggly stretch of toy-battle role-play more than plot.

title: The Voxor and the Exo-Tele
synopsis: A newly activated Voxor vehicle squares off against a rival fighter, with the narrators marveling at what an Exo-Tele could do by comparison. Masks get knocked loose and swapped between narrators mid-battle, and a countdown ticks toward a key return before the Voxor's power runs dry for the round.

title: Rendered Obsolete by the Exo-Toa
synopsis: A boastful Exo-Toa declares its abilities formidable enough to render its opponent's elemental powers obsolete, sparking an offended "why do you think I'm not a challenge" showdown. The narrators bring in a full lineup of challengers, including the Toa Nuva, before a vehicle rolls back in to needle everyone about who's really allowed to fight.

title: Snowball to the Face
synopsis: A long, sprawling battle stretch opens with someone getting smacked by a mock snowball and demanding a replacement mask after theirs flies clean across the field. Between weak-spot jokes, another "don't smoke, kids" cigar gag, and a wandering bit about a stolen arm, the wise Vakama steps in to call an opponent stupid before the vehicle chase resumes. It ends with a hunt for someone's missing tiny mask.

title: The Baloney Sandwich Standoff
synopsis: A telekinesis-and-vehicle skirmish gets derailed by a running joke about a "happy baloney sandwich" standing in for the looming Universal War. A masked servant of Makuta threatens to slash a rival to bits, but the fight dissolves into a search for a lost mask and its spirit, last seen blown off in the chaos.

title: Prophecy 26 and the Exotope
synopsis: A newly summoned Exotope creature enters the fray as the narrators debate weak spots, electric powers, and how to properly aim a "Raptor Rocket" at its mask. Bait, borrowed swords, and a swapped-out red mask keep the skirmish moving, capped by a silly threat to jam a sword down a rival's throat -- both of them.

title: Berries, Beans, and Super Confusion
synopsis: A trap springs and a barrage of watermelon and berry gags sends the battle into a giddy "charge up" frenzy, complete with a rapid-fire Confusion and Super Confusion exchange. One fighter starts pinning captured strength-masks to their own hand to steal their power, boasting "I have super strength!" as the skirmish winds down toward a near-knockout.

title: Prophecy 27 and the Gold Masks
synopsis: Talk turns to rare gold masks and a mysterious, more powerful ally as the narrators invoke a prophecy and its promised champion. A running bit about "mocking" versus making fun -- capped by a deadpan "what's two plus two? four" -- needles the villain, while masks and shields get knocked loose across a long, back-and-forth exchange.

title: The Koly Ball Kick-Off
synopsis: Between talk of surfing and a homemade "pizza monster," one fighter shows off turning their grabber claws into a fast-rolling koly ball for the fight. Masks pile up as trophies, kicks fly at varying strength "for the kids," and the segment closes on a chant of "I think I can" before the villain concedes defeat.

title: Don't Mistreat an Oyster
synopsis: Between armor swaps and a running joke about a mask that makes its wearer look noseless, the narrators debate the merits of gold masks supposedly coming soon to a mask shop. A mid-battle detour has one narrator literally rummaging through an attic for a sound effect, and the segment wraps with an oddly specific PSA: don't try this at home, and definitely don't mistreat an oyster.

title: Waka's Walnut Brain
synopsis: Makuta shows up looking different this time, now with a flying creature attached to his thigh and a pair of not-actually-tickling guns, as the narrators trade jabs about hollow heads and a rival's walnut-sized brain. A pesky flying bug briefly steals the spotlight before the fight's last attack gets teased and the segment cuts over to Stacy.

title: The Spirit of Destruction Revealed
synopsis: Dr. Seinyor faces down Makuta's true form, who reveals himself as the very Krana in front of them -- the self-proclaimed "spirit of destruction." A tense, surprisingly philosophical exchange follows about why destroying him would be self-defeating, needing only chaos, destruction, and war to win, before Dr. Seinyor claims special training and the battle finally begins.

title: Fighter Mode, Walking Mode
synopsis: The climactic showdown with Makuta escalates as the villain vows to escape and return within a year to unleash the Universal War if not destroyed now. Dr. Seinyor closes in for the finishing blow while a creature is sent in to "suck his soul out," and the fight cycles through dramatic mode-switches -- fighter mode, walking mode -- as a transformation begins.

title: Pay for What You've Done
synopsis: The final confrontation between Dr. Seinyor and Makuta replays and escalates, with the villain again threatening a year in hiding and a Universal War if he survives. A monstrous ally moves in to finish him off as the narrators call out "fighter mode" and "walking mode" over dramatic sound effects, ending on Makuta's defiant demand: "pay for what you've done to me."

title: See You at the AC
synopsis: In a brief closing beat, Makuta concedes total defeat -- "the Super Family has defeated me" -- and skulks off with a threat to return. The narrator signs off teasing the tenth movie and a coming war, promising to see everyone at the AC.

title: Breakfast, Fossils, and New Recruits
synopsis: Movie 10 opens with the usual ground rules and a roster of new toy recruits joining the family, including Bruisey and Whitestripe, a baby Bionicle and Tohunga, twin babies Jewelize and Emeril, and a batch of Transformers. The story then drops into a chaotic toy-family breakfast and schoolroom skit, complete with a math lesson and a running gag about a 'fossilized' pet lizard. It closes by setting up the real plot: the Toa and Turaga must scour the islands for platinum masks and mysterious silver crowns ahead of the coming Universal War.

title: Fossils, Bloopers, and Battle Plans
synopsis: More of the toy-family morning skit plays out, with the kids' 'dead pet lizard' turned into a cracked-skull show-and-tell and a late-night blooper moment before bed. The narrator then breaks in to explain the real mission: the Toa and Turaga must track down the Bohrok Kal and search for platinum masks and silver crowns, and battle plans start getting sketched out in the kitchen.

title: Charting the Search for the Bohrok Kal
synopsis: After a classroom detour, complete with a 'daily individual reading time' bit and a nail-painting break, the narrator lays toy figures out as map markers for the Toa and Turaga and dispatches them toward Ga-Koro and the other villages. A Toa suits up with a Krana and Kanohi mask and heads off in search of the Bohrok Kal, kicking off the real quest.

title: Awakening Tarnok Ka
synopsis: The narrator purifies a Krana to awaken and recruit a new Bohrok Kal ally, talked out of loyalty to the Barraki and into joining the Super Family. Night-vision Kanohi powers and a bit of hide-and-seek lead into the hunt for another Bohrok Kal, before the episode wraps with a costume-change musical number from the toy background singers.

title: The Waterfall Krana
synopsis: The hunt for another Bohrok Kal turns up a Krana tumbling down a waterfall instead, which the crew purifies and uses to awaken and recruit a new ally who agrees to defect from the Barraki. The search then moves into the jungle, where the group closes in on yet another Bohrok Kal to awaken.

title: Power Shields and New Allies
synopsis: A scrappy toy battle plays out over borrowed 'power shields' and locked-up weak spots, ending with another Bohrok Kal talked into abandoning the Barraki for the Super Family. A further new recruit is introduced before the narrator cues up the next big musical and dance number with the full cast of background singers.

title: Pop Live in Mexico
synopsis: A brief, mostly musical interlude built around a dance number introduced as 'Pop live in Mexico,' interrupted by a quick skirmish featuring one of the heroes showing off a plasma power and a shiny mask. It closes with another Bohrok Kal agreeing to join the Super Family.

title: The Last of the Bohrok Kal
synopsis: A goofy, gross-out battle full of jokes about who 'tastes like chicken wings' wraps up the Bohrok Kal hunt as the last holdouts are defeated and their masks swapped from gold to platinum. The narrator, in character as Tahu the Toa, gives a closing address thanking the audience and teasing the next movie: the coming Universal War and the mystery of the seventh Toa.
